Re  PRAYER : Criminal Original Petition filed under Section 4  Criminal Procedure Code, to call for the entire records pertaining   case in STC.No.13 of 2022 pending on the file of the learned Judici  Magistrate Vadipatti Madurai District and quash the same as against  petitioner. 
 For Petitioner : Mr.R.Anand  For Respondent : Mr.A.Albert James  Government Advocate (Crl. Si  1/6 https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis  Crl.O.P.(MD)No J.Thavamani Kumar vs The Food Safety Officer on 11 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/74402654/
1  ORDER This petition has been filed to quash the proceedings pending in STC.No.13 of 2022 on the file of the learned Judicial Magistrate, Vadipatti, Madurai District. 
2.The respondent has filed a private complaint against the petitioner for offence under Sections 51,
58 and 59(i) of the 'Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006' (hereinafter referred to as 'the Act' for brevity). The allegation made in the complaint is that on 13.05.2020 at about 11.15 a.m., an inspection was conducted by the Food Safety Officer in the shop belonging to the petitioner and gingelly oil in loose condition was drawn as a sample in four packets. Thereafter, it was sent for test to the food analyst on 14.05.2020 which was received on 18.05.2020 and the report dated 30.07.2020 was issued stating that the sample is sub- standard and unsafe and prohibitions and restrictions on sales. On receipt of the report, the designated officer sent his recommendation on 10.08.2020 to the Commissioner for initiation of prosecution. On receipt of the sanction, the private complaint came to be filed before the Court https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis Crl.O.P.(MD)No.18261 of 2022 below. 
3.Heard the learned counsel for the petitioner and the learned Government Advocate appearing on behalf of the respondent. 
4.Apart from other grounds that were raised by the learned counsel for the petitioner, the main ground that was raised was that the petitioner was denied an opportunity of sending the sample for further test as provided under Section 46(4) of the Act. This is in view of the fact that a communication dated 07.08.2020 was sent by the designated officer directing the petitioner to avail his right within a period of 30 days for sending the sample for referral. However, this communication was posted only on 25.09.2020. In the mean time, the order of sanction was issued on 10.08.2020 and the private complaint was filed. 
5.The above procedural infirmity is clearly in violation of the provisions of the Act and it took away the right available to the petitioner to send the sample for referral. The sanction was granted in this case even before the expiry of the time that was given to the petitioner to send the sample for referral. https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis Crl.O.P.(MD)No.18261 of 2022 6.In view of the above, the continuation of the criminal proceedings as against the petitioner will result in abuse of process of law and the same requires the interference of this Court. 
7.In the result, the proceedings in STC.No.13 of 2022 on the file of the learned Judicial Magistrate,
Vadipatti, is hereby quashed and this Criminal Original Petition stands allowed. Consequently,
connected miscellaneous petition is closed.
